name: @omp-dev-team/token-diet
description: Wires lean-ctx into Oh-My-Pi: bash/read/grep/find/ls are routed through it for large token savings, plus the caveman output-brevity skill.
comment: v3.0.0 replaces ctx-wire with lean-ctx (github.com/yvgude/lean-ctx, MIT). ctx-wire compressed COMMAND OUTPUT only, so this plugin carried a hand-written TOML filter pack for the four dotnet commands OMP's shellMinimizer misses. lean-ctx supersedes that: it compresses command output AND file reads, search results and project context, recognises 75+ tools, and keeps a session cache so an unchanged re-read costs a handful of tokens. The routing itself is upstream's pi-lean-ctx extension, mirrored from npm by install.sh rather than vendored - it declares pi.extensions, which OMP still accepts (docs/extension-loading.md:42,142), has zero dependencies, and uses only APIs OMP implements. context-compress and its protect/messages libs went with ctx-wire: lean-ctx does that job better and ours was off by default anyway. What is left here is the wiring, the caveman skill (output tokens, which lean-ctx does not address) and path-inject (OMP's shell snapshot runs `bash -c`, which sources no profile, so ~/.local/bin tooling stays invisible).
